newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- higher with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- higher with Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were higher at midday following the Treasury market, but traders complained that little cash is available for secondary action.
Several bid-wanted lists in the morning kept the market from gaining strongly, but traders said prices were up as much as 1/2 point in early afternoon action.
Those gains lag the Treasury market, where technical factors were given credit for the improvement. The long bond was up 20/32 at 94-25/32 to yield 7.05 percent.
New issue action was sparse, though Morgan Stanley & Co. said it repriced Tucson Electric Power Co.'s $132 million revenue bond deal. The top yield at the repricing was 7.125 percent in 2032.

The futures markets are also reflecting the stronger tone, with the June municipal contract up 17/32 to 112-26/32 and June T-bonds 21/32 higher at 108-4/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 150 ticks from 154 at the close on Wednesday.

In secondary market activity, Delaware River Port Authority FGIC-insured 5-1/2s of 2026 were bid at 5.86 percent, up one basis point. Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were up 1/8 at 96-5/8.
Economic data Thursday included the February trade gap, of $11.59 billion. Wall Street economnists had forecast a deficit of $10.1 billion.

The U.S. Department of Labor said initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted, rose to 332,000 the week ended April 12 from a revised 324,000 prior week. Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 317,000.
